name: Rahm Emanuel
role: US representative (2003–2009), White House chief of staff (2009–2010), Chicago mayor (2011–2019), and ambassador to Japan (2022–2025)
summary: Emanuel combines market-oriented economic development with public investment, higher minimum wages and expanded education access. He supports US alliances and deterrence, while his recent proposals would condition relations with Israel and end its US defense subsidy. His policing and school reforms have generated substantial controversy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 2006 book set universal affordable coverage as an ultimate objective reached in steps, and he drove the Affordable Care Act as chief of staff, but he also called single-payer Medicare for All untenable; the evidence points both ways on government provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He strongly supports the $13 minimum wage and inflation-linked increases.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His 2006 book proposed restoring the capital gains tax for the wealthy and objected that a millionaire's trading gains are taxed below a secretary's wages; he also voted against the 2003 tax-cut bill and permanent estate-tax repeal. He did not call for large across-the-board increases.

unions-good.rationale: Mixed record: he voted for the Employee Free Choice Act in 2007, but as mayor he fought the Chicago Teachers Union, backed Illinois SB 7 limits on teacher strikes, and later said he erred by revoking the teachers' final-year raise.
